findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (RCS 758)
findings.note: Voted aye on second reading (66 aye, 47 no). Ratified text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) adds new G.S. 163-83: a county board processes a registration only if it affirmatively says the applicant is a US citizen, and a form with no answer gets a 30-day notice and a sworn citizenship statement or the registration is denied. It also has the State Board set up a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database. The bill page shows a Governor's veto and a last action of placed on calendar for 09/02/2026.
NC House, Third Reading (roll call #810), 2024-12-11: yea (tally 73–45); census gate: none.
subjects: photo ID for all voters (constitutional amendment, in person and by mail)

findings.motion: House roll call 758, HB 958 Election Law Changes, second reading, passed 66-47
findings.note: Official House roll call transcript lists him among the Ayes. The version voted on (fifth edition) keeps photo ID for in-person voting and provisional ballots counted only if photo ID is shown to the county board, lengthens the time to show it to five business days, sets a similar ID fix for voters whose driver license or Social Security digits do not match, and treats a missing ID photocopy with an absentee ballot as a curable defect.
